title: Manufacturing and Production Work
description: Types of Accidents and Injuries You Might Suffer Factory Jobs Often Involve Tough, Repetitive Work And Exposure To Serious Hazards. Some Of The Most Common Causes Of Injury Include Repetitive Motion : Tasks done over and over can cause you carpal tunnel, tendonitis, bursitis, and other painful soft tissue injuries. Overexertion: Repeated heavy lifting and physically demanding work can lead to muscle and bone problems. Body Movement Strain: Constant crawling, twisting, reaching, and bending can wear down your body over time. Forklift accidents: These machines are essential, but you can be seriously hurt if pinned or caught in the equipment. Harmful Substances: Being exposed to chemicals and toxins can cause burns, lung problems, or other long-term illnesses. Equipment & Objects: Heavy machinery can crush, cut, or even lead to amputations in the event of an accident. Fires & Explosions: Flammable materials can quickly turn a small fire into a deadly blaze. Because of these risks, you face injuries such as amputations, broken bones, spinal cord damage, burns, toxic exposure illnesses, respiratory problems, hearing or vision loss, and more on your job. Some injuries may heal with time and treatment, while others can cause permanent disability. title: epoxy
description: Company Description Annoushka Jewellery is a contemporary jewelry brand recognized for its distinctive designs and meticulous craftsmanship. The company focuses on creating pieces that combine artistic expression with high-quality materials, appealing to clients who value originality and attention to detail. Team members work in a creative, fast-paced environment where precision and reliability are essential. Annoushka Jewellery encourages collaboration, continuous learning, and pride in producing exceptional products. Joining the team offers the opportunity to contribute directly to the creation of unique jewelry pieces and to grow within a specialized craft. Role Description The epoxy role at Annoushka Jewellery is a full-time, on-site position based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This role involves preparing and mixing epoxy resins according to specific formulas and quality standards, and applying epoxy to jewelry components to ensure a durable, polished finish. Day-to-day tasks include measuring materials accurately, monitoring curing times, checking for defects or imperfections, and making necessary adjustments to maintain consistency and quality. The role also includes cleaning and maintaining workstations and tools, following safety procedures, and collaborating with designers and production staff to meet order deadlines. The person in this role will be expected to follow detailed instructions, maintain high attention to detail, and support continuous improvements in the finishing process. Qualifications Ability to work with epoxy and similar materials, including accurate measuring, mixing, and application for small, detailed items. Strong attention to detail and quality control, with the ability to identify imperfections and ensure a consistent, high-quality finish. Basic understanding of safe handling of chemicals and adherence to workplace health and safety guidelines. Good hand–eye coordination and manual dexterity for fine, detailed work in jewelry production. Effective communication and teamwork skills to collaborate with production and design teams. Reliability and time management skills to meet production schedules and deadlines. Prior experience in jewelry making, resin art, crafts, or similar precision manufacturing is an advantage. Willingness to learn specialized techniques and follow structured processes and quality standards.

title: Education Abroad Advisor
description: Apply now Job no: 507009 Work type: Full-Time Location: Hybrid/Flexible Work Arrangement Categories: Drexel University, Global, Interprofessional, and Specialized Programming Job Summary The Education Abroad Advisor is responsible for promoting education abroad programs to students and stakeholders, advising and supporting students before, during, and after their study abroad experience, and administering select Drexel education abroad programs in select regions of the world. Regional responsibility includes France, Belgium, Switzerland, Spain, and Latin America, though ultimately will be based upon the needs of the Education Abroad team. The Education Abroad Advisor also manages and advises faculty and students on non-credit experiences abroad (NCEAs), which include international service learning, research, athletics, and conferences. The advisor provides guidance on the NCEA application process, facilitates group info sessions and pre-departure support. The Education Abroad Advisor is responsible for the annual review of regional responsibility program brochures and initial creation of new brochures in collaboration with the Associate Director. The advisor has additional administrative duties including, but is not limited to the following: Online pre-departure orientation Being the primary liaison with Drexel’s Enrollment Management and Student Success office and taking the lead on various events, including accepted student days, welcome week, etc. Curriculum integration Additional projects to contribute to the operations of the office will be assigned according to office needs Occasional nights and weekends required Domestic and international travel may be required Essential Functions Recruiting and advising students on study abroad programs in assigned regions of the world Advising students and faculty through the non-credit experience abroad approval process Communicating with various education abroad stakeholders including administrative and academic departments across campus as well as foreign contacts Attending relevant university events and making presentations pertaining to their portfolio of education abroad opportunities as well as education abroad in general Developing marketing campaigns, events, and sessions to recruit students Attending various regional and national conferences and represent Drexel Global at various university events Managing and developing content for the outbound pre-departure orientation Managing curriculum integration efforts in assigned academic area Participating in site visits in support of their program portfolio Providing coverage when other staff members are out of the office Other duties as assigned Required Qualifications Minimum of a Bachelor's Degree or the equivalent combination of education and work experience. (Please review the Equivalency Chart for additional information.) Minimum of 2 years of experience working in international education, preferably education abroad Must be a self-starter and flexibility Ability to set goals and complete projects with a high degree of independence Ability to communicate persuasively, attention to detail, and ability to handle several tasks at once are essential for this job Preferred Qualifications Master’s Degree Experience living, working, and/or studying abroad, preferably in a French or Spanish speaking location Ability to speak another language Knowledge of educational systems of other countries Experience with Banner, MS Office suite, and/or Terra Dotta Software Physical Demands Typically sitting at a desk/table Location Hybrid/Flexible Work Arrangement Additional Information This position is classified as Exempt, grade I. Compensation for this grade ranges from $ 45,330.00 to $ 68,000.00 per year. Please note that the offered rate for this position will vary based on the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience, department budget, and an internal equity review. Applicants are encouraged to explore the Professional Staff salary structure and Compensation Guidelines & Policies for more details on Drexel’s compensation framework. For information about benefits, please review Drexel’s Benefits Brochure. Special Instructions to the Applicant Please make sure you upload your CV/resume and cover letter when submitting your application. A review of applicants will begin once a suitable candidate pool is identified. title: MEAL Officer
description: JOB DESCRIPTION The Opportunity The MEAL Officer will be responsible for monitoring project activities, including conducting post-distribution monitoring and supporting project assessments in close collaboration with data collectors. The role also involves supporting external evaluation processes, ensuring the effective implementation of accountability systems in project intervention areas, and capturing learning insights for the field office under the Strengthening Climate Resilience through the Integrated Landscape Project , in close coordination with the project field team The MEAL Officer will be responsible for collecting essential performance monitoring data, conducting quality benchmark monitoring, and preparing monthly accomplishment reports for submission to the MEAL Coordinator. Furthermore, he/she will support and facilitate MEAL-related tasks in collaboration with the MEAL team to ensure the timely delivery of activities with the desired quality standard. KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY: (MEAL officer) Job Specific Roles And Responsibilities Finalize and operationalize the MEAL Plan, IPTT, SOPs, aligning indicators with PMF/logical frameworks of the project Finalize and operationalize other MEAL toolkits, such as MEAL PIRS, Action Tracker, Feedback Tracker, and Quality Benchmarks Develop and update MEAL plan and log frame on PRIME, ensuring indicator progress and means of verification are adequately updated by project teams. Lead set-up of database design, digital data collection (Kobo), data management pipelines, and Power BI dashboards for near real-time performance monitoring. Establish Data Quality Assurance (DQA) procedures and verification sampling frames Reporting Oversee routine monitoring cycles, ensuring completeness, timeliness, and disaggregation (gender, age, inclusion, and participation of women, youth, children, and persons with disabilities in project‑relevant activities and decision‑making. Design and implement DQAs, spot checks, back-checks, and collect the relevant beneficiaries' data from project livelihood officers. Supervise the project progress with a standard checklist in project intervention kebeles and triangulate among their monthly progress reports, then identify data quality gaps. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Minimum Qualifications and Experience Required Essential: BA/BSC Degree in Monitoring & Evaluation, Statistics, Agriculture, Livelihoods, Rural Development, Economics, advanced degree preferred. 3 years MEAL experience in livelihoods, economic empowerment or market systems programs, with at least 2 years directly to FSL projects. Strong practical experience with digital data collection tools (Kobo/ODK), data management systems, and dashboarding tools. KNOWLEDGE SKILLS AND ABILITY Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in difficult environments Experience in pastoral contexts, preferably Afar region; knowledge of the Afar language mandatory Excellent report writing and English proficiency.
